# Ang Totoong Narcolist

## Genesis and Content of the Video Series

The "Ang Totoong Narcolist" phenomenon emerged in the Philippines in early 2019 as a viral YouTube-based video series that ignited a significant political firestorm . The project was the work of Peter Joemel Advincula, who operated under the alias "Bikoy" , . The series consisted of five videos uploaded between April 2, 2019, and May 6, 2019, though some sources note an upload timeline ending on April 22, 2019 , . These videos were hosted on a YouTube channel also named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" and presented themselves as a confessional exposé by a former member of a powerful illegal drug syndicate . The narration, delivered by a hooded Advincula, detailed his purported experiences working within the organization, claiming he had started as a CCTV operator, then progressed to scanning the tattoos of senior syndicate members, and ultimately handled the depositing of drug money , . This self-presentation lent an air of authenticity to the allegations, positioning him as an insider with firsthand knowledge.

The content of the videos was explosive, directly accusing several prominent individuals aligned with the administration of President Rodrigo Duterte of complicity in the illegal drug trade . Among the most high-profile figures targeted were members of the Duterte family and their close associates. Specifically, the videos accused Paolo Duterte, the president's son; Waldo Carpio, the brother-in-law of First Lady Sara Duterte; Honeylet Avanceña, another relative of the First Lady; and her daughter Kitty Duterte of being patrons of the syndicate , . Episode 4 of the series explicitly named Paolo Duterte, Veronica Salvador, Bong Go, and Mans Carpio as "main players from the Davao side" of a supposed "Tausug drug group" . The narrator claimed he had personally scanned the alleged syndicate tattoos of these individuals at the Misibis Bay resort in Albay .

Further accusations extended to Senator Christopher "Bong" Go, who served as a Special Assistant to the President (SAP) at the time , . The videos also implicated businessman Elizaldy Co, whose resort was mentioned as a location for the syndicate's activities . In one instance, Advincula even stated his intention to sue Paolo Duterte, Bong Go, and Manases Carpio for defamation . The entire series was framed around the existence of a sophisticated drug operation, referred to at times as the "Quadrangle Drug Syndicate," allegedly operating out of the Misibis Bay resort . The production of these videos appears to have been carefully staged and coordinated. According to an affidavit filed by Advincula, the meetings related to the creation of the videos, dubbed "Project Sodoma," began in August 2018 . Video shooting commenced on March 29, 2019, inside the Jesuit Communications Building (Jescom) at Ateneo de Manila University (ADMU) . The first video was uploaded on April 1, 2019, and the final video was uploaded on April 22, 2019 . Notably, the videos were uploaded using the ADMU server, specifically the "Guest 1" SSID attached to the university's Management Information System, from a room inside the faculty housing compound .

Advincula's credibility as the source of these revelations was immediately questioned due to his personal history. Born on March 22, 1989, in Donsol, Sorsogon, he was identified as a convicted fraudster . He had served a six-year prison sentence for fraud, which he completed and from which he was released early in 2017 . This background cast a shadow over his claims, establishing a baseline of skepticism regarding his motives and reliability. Furthermore, his narrative contained elements of continuity with past political conflicts. In a December 2016 document he authored, known as the "Sotto document," Advincula had previously accused officials from the preceding administration, including then-President Benigno Aquino III, Interior Secretary Mar Roxas, and Senator Leila de Lima, of meeting with the same syndicate figure, Elizaldy "Zaldy" Co, at the Misibis Bay Resort . This earlier document, however, was unnotarized and lacked the detail present in his later "Bikoy" videos, where these Aquino-era figures were conspicuously absent from the list of accused patrons, replaced instead by Duterte-aligned politicians and businessmen . This shift in targets added another layer of complexity and potential inconsistency to his overall story.

## Institutional Responses and Political Polarization

The release of the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" videos triggered an immediate and deeply polarized response from various branches of the Philippine government, revealing a stark division in how to interpret and act upon politically charged allegations. The reactions ranged from swift endorsement and prosecution to cautious dismissal and outright condemnation, reflecting the intense political climate surrounding the Duterte administration. The Department of Justice (DOJ) initiated an investigation into the videos on April 17, 2019, signaling official scrutiny . However, the most aggressive institutional response came from the Philippine National Police (PNP). Under the leadership of Chief General Oscar Albayalde, the PNP Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) treated the allegations with serious credence. On an unspecified date in 2019, following the videos' release and Advincula's initial public appearance, Albayalde stated that the accusations leveled by "Bikoy" were "substantially accurate" . He further asserted that these claims were supported by "other documentary evidence and other sources" gathered by the CIDG, which had already begun filing criminal charges against several opposition figures . Based on this assessment, the PNP filed a sweeping set of complaints—including sedition, inciting to sedition, cyberlibel, libel, estafa (fraud), harboring a criminal, and obstruction of justice—against Vice President Leni Robredo and 34 other individuals linked to the opposition , . The charges were explicitly grounded in Advincula’s testimony and the documentary evidence collected by the CIDG, with the PNP chief emphasizing that the ultimate assessment of a witness's credibility rested with the courts, not with the police itself .

In contrast to the PNP's enthusiastic endorsement, the DOJ, led by Secretary Menardo Guevarra, adopted a more measured and procedural approach. While advancing the investigation, Guevarra clarified that the decision to grant Peter Joemel Advincula provisional protection under the Witness Protection Program (WPP) would depend on the DOJ's evaluation of his credibility as a prosecution witness . He confirmed that Advincula could receive such protection upon submitting a sworn affidavit and formally applying for the program, but stressed that the DOJ's evaluation was pending . This cautious stance was mirrored by the legislative branch. Senator Panfilo Lacson, then chair of the Senate Committee on Public Order and Dangerous Drugs, announced on April 9, 2019, that his committee was prepared to schedule a hearing on Advincula's allegations "within this week" . However, this readiness was conditional; Lacson stipulated that Advincula must first personally present a sworn statement and verifiable supporting evidence, such as bank documents or wire transfer records, to substantiate his accusations against the president's inner circle . This demand for concrete proof highlighted a critical procedural check-and-balance mechanism that stood in tension with the PNP's more direct acceptance of Advincula's narrative.

The executive branch, through Malacañang Palace, responded with a preemptive counter-narrative that quickly labeled the entire affair a deliberate political conspiracy. Presidential Spokesperson Salvador Panelo announced the discovery of an "Oust Duterte" matrix on April 22, 2019, which listed journalists and opposition figures allegedly involved in plots to remove the president . He later revealed a "deliberate conspiracy" orchestrated by the Liberal Party (LP) and the Magdalo group, characterizing the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" videos as an election-related gambit designed to discredit the Duterte family . Communications Secretary Martin Andanar and Panelo subsequently named specific co-conspirators, including Gary Alejano, Manuel Roxas, and Edwin Lacierda . The administration's executive branch effectively shut down any potential for a neutral legislative inquiry before it could even begin. Following Advincula's public unmasking at the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) office on May 6, 2019, Senate President Vicente Sotto III declared that Advincula had previously attempted to peddle similar falsehoods against officials from the Aquino administration, labeling him a "gun-for-hire" . This characterization was echoed by Senate Minority Leader Franklin Drilon, who dismissed Advincula's subsequent recantation as "ridiculous" and called for charges to be filed against him . The cancellation of the scheduled Senate hearing on May 8, 2019, marked the end of any formal legislative process, solidifying the administration's position that the issue was closed and the accuser was a discredited figure , . This institutional polarization demonstrated how state apparatuses became tools in a larger political battle, with the PNP pursuing prosecutions based on a controversial witness while the executive and legislative branches worked to delegitimize both the witness and the allegations themselves.

## The Recantation and the Project Sodoma Narrative

The trajectory of the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" saga took a dramatic and pivotal turn on May 6, 2019, when Peter Joemel Advincula publicly revealed himself as the hooded narrator "Bikoy" during a news conference at the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) office , , . Initially, he reiterated his support for the original allegations, standing by the accusations made in the videos against individuals close to President Duterte , . However, this public declaration was short-lived. Just days later, on May 22-23, 2019, Advincula surrendered to authorities at Camp Crame and retracted all his previous statements , . In a stunning reversal, he claimed that the entire "Ang Totoong Narcolist" series was a fabrication, orchestrated by the Liberal Party and Senator Antonio Trillanes IV as part of a larger, coordinated political operation , , . This new narrative introduced the concept of "Project Sodoma," a code name for what he described as a concerted effort by the opposition to destabilize the Duterte administration and orchestrate an ousting plot , .

Under this revised account, the goal of "Project Sodoma" was to install Vice President Leni Robredo as president and Antonio Trillanes as vice president . Advincula alleged that he was promised a ₱500,000 payment for his participation and claimed the videos were part of a script written by the Liberal Party , . This pivot transformed the entire affair from a matter of public interest into a high-stakes political confrontation centered on the accusation of conspiracy versus the defense of innocence. Advincula shifted from being a witness providing explosive testimony to becoming the primary suspect in a potential crime, facing charges of perjury for his contradictory statements. His new claims required a complete reversal of the existing narrative, demanding that the very institutions that had pursued charges against the opposition now investigate him and his new accusers. To bolster his new story, Advincula submitted two CIDG affidavits dated May 29, 2019, and July 17, 2019, which explicitly linked "Project Sodoma" to the opposition and were used to support the inciting-to-sedition complaint filed on August 9, 2019 against a wide array of opposition figures .

This recantation and the introduction of the "Project Sodoma" theory had profound consequences. It forced a re-evaluation of the initial wave of criminal complaints filed by the PNP. The credibility of the entire case against the opposition crumbled with the withdrawal of its primary witness. The administration, which had initially positioned itself to defend the president's family, was now faced with a claim that the entire scandal was a manufactured attack. The opposition figures who had been charged with sedition, cyberlibel, and other crimes found their legal situation fundamentally altered. They were no longer just defendants in a case brought by a whistleblower; they were now accused of being the architects of a massive conspiracy involving a disgraced informant. Businessman Elizaldy Co, whose resort was mentioned in the original videos, filed a separate cyber libel complaint seeking over ₱1 billion in damages against Advincula, Facebook, and YouTube for the false accusations . The situation created a complex legal and political quagmire, with each side presenting a compelling but mutually exclusive narrative. The government's institutions were now tasked with investigating whether Advincula's recantation was genuine or another fabricated lie, adding another layer of uncertainty to an already volatile situation. The episode underscored the fragility of truth in highly politicized environments and demonstrated how easily a narrative can be flipped from an exposé into an allegation of conspiracy, with devastating implications for all parties involved.

## Legal Proceedings and Unresolved Charges

The legal fallout from the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" videos was extensive and prolonged, resulting in a complex web of criminal complaints, dismissals, and protracted court battles. Immediately following the release of the videos, the Philippine National Police (PNP) Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) filed a comprehensive set of charges against Vice President Leni Robredo and 34 other prominent opposition figures . These charges included sedition, inciting to sedition, cyberlibel, libel, estafa (fraud), harboring a criminal, and obstruction of justice, all explicitly grounded in the testimony and revelations provided by Peter Joemel Advincula , . A Quezon City court issued an arrest order for Antonio Trillanes IV and ten others on February 14, 2020, for their alleged involvement in "conspiracy to commit sedition" . Trillanes promptly posted bail on February 18, 2020, and subsequently challenged the legality of the charges . On October 19, 2020, Trillanes filed a Motion to Quash the Information, arguing that the charging document was legally defective for failing to provide specific factual details establishing the elements of conspiracy or sedition, thereby violating his constitutional right to be informed of the nature of the accusation . This motion, joined by co-accused Joselito Saracho, sought a dismissal of the case to prevent a protracted trial on a void charging document, highlighting the ongoing legal challenges that kept the case active in the courts well into late 2020 .

Despite the flurry of activity from the PNP and the judiciary, the Department of Justice (DOJ) eventually took a decisive step that significantly altered the legal landscape. On February 10, 2020, the DOJ officially dismissed the cases of sedition, cyberlibel, libel, estafa, harboring a criminal, and obstruction of justice that had been filed against Vice President Leni Robredo and 23 other individuals, including senators, religious leaders, and lawyers . The dismissal was based on a finding of lack of probable cause . This resolution effectively cleared the primary targets of the initial wave of accusations and dealt a major blow to the administration's legal strategy. However, the dismissal of these cases did not bring the legal proceedings to a definitive close. The case against Antonio Trillanes IV remained in limbo, with arraignment delays continuing due to motions to quash as of October 22, 2020 . The DOJ's resolution in the main case was later cited in a broader context on February 10, 2025, which charged 11 respondents, including Advincula and Trillanes, with conspiracy to commit sedition under Article 141 of the Revised Penal Code, indicating the enduring legal weight of the affair .

Peter Joemel Advincula himself did not escape legal repercussions for his actions. His career as a political actor was fraught with legal troubles stemming from the scandal. In January 2021, he was charged with perjury for his contradictory statements regarding the videos . Later, in November 2021, he faced murder charges related to the so-called "Albay killings" . These charges, along with his conviction for fraud, painted a picture of a man with a troubled legal history who leveraged a national political scandal for his own purposes. Despite these issues, Advincula continued to be involved in the political sphere. After being disqualified by the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) in October 2024, he filed as a nuisance candidate for the 2025 Senate election, demonstrating his persistence in trying to maintain a political presence . The legal aftermath thus reveals a messy and unresolved conclusion. While the administration failed to secure convictions against its political opponents, it successfully launched damaging legal proceedings that tied up their time and resources for years. Conversely, the opposition figures, particularly Trillanes, remained entangled in a protracted legal battle, illustrating the long-term costs of being ensnared in such politically motivated attacks. The saga ended not with a clean victory for either side, but with a series of partial victories and ongoing legal disputes that reflected the deep divisions within the country's justice system.

## Credibility Controversies and Inconsistencies

The entire "Ang Totoong Narcolist" affair was fundamentally undermined by persistent questions regarding the credibility of its creator, Peter Joemel Advincula, and the glaring inconsistencies within his own narratives. From the outset, his background as a convicted fraudster with a six-year prison sentence, released early in 2017, cast a long shadow over his claims . This history established a baseline of suspicion that his motives were questionable. This skepticism was further fueled by his own admission that he had a history of attempting to sell false information to law enforcement agencies for payment. On May 8, 2019, Philippine National Police (PNP) Chief Gen. Oscar Albayalde publicly labeled Advincula an "information peddler," citing two prior instances where Advincula allegedly offered false information to police for sums ranging from ₱40,000 to ₱70,000 but failed to deliver or provided baseless claims . This characterization directly contradicted the PNP chief's earlier statement that Advincula's initial accusations were "substantially accurate" and severely damaged his reputation as a reliable witness , .

Beyond his personal history, a detailed analysis by VERA Files Fact Check exposed recurring themes, missing information, and glaring inconsistencies across Advincula's various pronouncements and sworn statements . One of the most significant contradictions was the shifting target of his accusations. In a December 2016 document he wrote, the "Sotto document," Advincula had accused officials from the preceding Aquino administration, including President Benigno Aquino III, Interior Secretary Mar Roxas, and Senator Leila de Lima, of having meetings with the drug syndicate figure Elizaldy "Zaldy" Co . However, in his May 6, 2019 affidavit and press briefing detailing the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" videos, these Aquino-era figures were entirely omitted from his list of accused patrons. Instead, his focus shifted entirely to Duterte-aligned figures, naming Paolo Duterte and Bong Go as the syndicate's patrons in the Davao area . This abrupt change in targets raised serious questions about the factual basis of his claims and suggested that his accusations might be tailored to fit a current political agenda rather than reflecting a consistent reality. The fact-checking analysis concluded that his accounts of the drug syndicate's structure and operations varied significantly across different affidavits and press conferences, further eroding confidence in his narrative .

The controversy also spilled over into the realm of traditional media. When the "matrix" report accusing journalists and opposition figures of plotting to oust President Duterte surfaced, the Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism (PCIJ) issued a strong denial. PCIJ executive director Malou Mangahas stated that the organization did not receive any email from Vera Files president Ellen Tordesillas about the videos, denied posting or distributing any stories related to them, and confirmed that the video was originally accessed by the public via YouTube . She emphasized that PCIJ is a non-stock, independent media organization and warned that those behind the "matrix" may have committed a crime by invading privacy through unauthorized access to journalists' emails . This clarification was crucial in distinguishing legitimate investigative journalism from the unsubstantiated allegations circulating online. The combination of Advincula's questionable background, his admitted propensity for peddling false information, and the demonstrable inconsistencies in his own stories created a mountain of evidence against his credibility. This body of evidence provided objective support for the conclusions reached by critics like Senator Panfilo Lacson, who had dismissed the entire episode as "nonsense" and Advincula as a "gun-for-hire" even before the full extent of the inconsistencies became public , . Ultimately, the credibility crisis surrounding Peter Joemel Advincula was the single most important factor in the collapse of the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" scandal, transforming it from a potential political earthquake into a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked misinformation.

## Aftermath and Enduring Legacy

The "Ang Totoong Narcolist" saga concluded without a clear victor, leaving a complex and lasting legacy that reshaped the political landscape of the Philippines and left deep scars on its institutions. The most immediate outcome was the failure of the Duterte administration to secure convictions against its political opponents. The Department of Justice's dismissal of the sedition and other charges against Vice President Leni Robredo and 23 others on February 10, 2020, for lack of probable cause, represented a significant legal and political defeat for the executive branch . This outcome signaled that even in a highly charged political environment, the standard of probable cause and judicial review could serve as a formidable barrier to politically motivated prosecutions. However, the administration was not without success. By launching these damaging legal proceedings, it succeeded in tying up the time and resources of prominent opposition figures for years, creating a chilling effect and forcing them to divert attention from policy-making to defending themselves in court. The protracted legal battles, particularly the ongoing challenge to the charges against Antonio Trillanes IV, exemplified the long-term strategic cost of being targeted in such a manner , .

For Peter Joemel Advincula, the affair cemented his reputation as a controversial and unreliable figure, yet it also propelled him back into the public eye and allowed him to pursue his own political ambitions. Despite being charged with perjury in January 2021 and murder in November 2021, he continued to be a fixture in Philippine politics . His attempt to file as a nuisance candidate for the 2025 Senate election, even after being disqualified by the COMELEC, demonstrates his resilience and his ability to leverage the notoriety gained from the scandal to remain relevant . His journey from a convicted fraudster and "information peddler" to a key player in a national political drama illustrates the blurred lines between fact, fiction, and political opportunism in modern Philippine society.

Perhaps the most enduring aspect of the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" affair is the persistence of the "Project Sodoma" conspiracy theory in the nation's political lexicon. Although unsubstantiated and largely debunked, the term has become a shorthand for describing perceived anti-government plots. This demonstrates how powerful ideas and narratives can endure long after the specific facts that gave rise to them have crumbled. The incident serves as a stark case study on the weaponization of law and technology. It showcased how legal tools like sedition and cyberlibel could be deployed as instruments of political warfare against opponents, while digital platforms like YouTube could be used to bypass traditional media gatekeepers and spread explosive allegations directly to a mass audience , . The use of a prestigious institution like Ateneo de Manila University's server to host the videos added another layer of complexity, implicating academic and religious spaces in the political fray and raising questions about accountability .

In summary, the legacy of "Ang Totoong Narcolist" is multifaceted. It exposed the deep polarization within the Philippines' state institutions, revealing how they could be mobilized to serve opposing political ends. It highlighted the immense power and danger of social media as a tool for political mobilization and disinformation. Most importantly, it left a lasting imprint on the country's political discourse, embedding concepts like "narco-politics" and "ouster plots" as permanent features of the political debate. The saga stands as a testament to the fragility of truth in a hyper-partisan environment and serves as a critical lesson on the importance of due process, credible evidence, and journalistic integrity in navigating the turbulent waters of modern democracy.

Senate Minority Leader Franklin Drilon dismissed Advincula's subsequent recantation as "ridiculous".
Senate Minority Leader Franklin Drilon called for charges to be filed against Advincula.
The scheduled Senate hearing on May 8, 2019, was canceled.
The cancellation of the Senate hearing marked the end of any formal legislative process regarding the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" allegations.
The cancellation solidified the administration's position that the issue was closed.
The cancellation solidified the administration's position that the accuser (Advincula) was a discredited figure.
The trajectory of the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" saga took a dramatic and pivotal turn on May 6, 2019.
Peter Joemel Advincula publicly revealed himself as the hooded narrator "Bikoy" during a news conference at the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) office on May 6, 2019.
Initially, Peter Joemel Advincula reiterated his support for the original allegations made in the videos.
Peter Joemel Advincula stood by the accusations made in the videos against individuals close to President Duterte.
On May 22-23, 2019, Peter Joemel Advincula surrendered to authorities at Camp Crame.
Peter Joemel Advincula retracted all his previous statements regarding the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" videos.
Peter Joemel Advincula claimed that the entire "Ang Totoong Narcolist" series was a fabrication.
Peter Joemel Advincula claimed the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" series was orchestrated by the Liberal Party and Senator Antonio Trillanes IV.
Peter Joemel Advincula claimed the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" series was part of a larger, coordinated political operation.
Advincula's new narrative introduced the concept of "Project Sodoma".
"Project Sodoma" was a code name for what Advincula described as a concerted effort by the opposition to destabilize the Duterte administration.
"Project Sodoma" was a code name for what Advincula described as a concerted effort by the opposition to orchestrate an ousting plot.
Under Advincula's revised account, the goal of "Project Sodoma" was to install Vice President Leni Robredo as president.
Under Advincula's revised account, the goal of "Project Sodoma" was to install Antonio Trillanes as vice president.
Advincula alleged that he was promised a ₱500,000 payment for his participation in "Project Sodoma".
Advincula claimed the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" videos were part of a script written by the Liberal Party.
To bolster his new story, Advincula submitted two CIDG affidavits dated May 29, 2019, and July 17, 2019.
The CIDG affidavits explicitly linked "Project Sodoma" to the opposition.
The CIDG affidavits were used to support the inciting-to-sedition complaint filed on August 9, 2019, against a wide array of opposition figures.
Businessman Elizaldy Co filed a separate cyber libel complaint seeking over ₱1 billion in damages against Advincula, Facebook, and YouTube for the false accusations.

Immediately following the release of the videos, the Philippine National Police (PNP) Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) filed a comprehensive set of charges against Vice President Leni Robredo and 34 other prominent opposition figures.
The charges included sedition, inciting to sedition, cyberlibel, libel, estafa (fraud), harboring a criminal, and obstruction of justice.
All charges were explicitly grounded in the testimony and revelations provided by Peter Joemel Advincula.
A Quezon City court issued an arrest order for Antonio Trillanes IV and ten others on February 14, 2020, for their alleged involvement in "conspiracy to commit sedition".
Trillanes promptly posted bail on February 18, 2020.
Trillanes subsequently challenged the legality of the charges.
On October 19, 2020, Trillanes filed a Motion to Quash the Information.
Trillanes argued that the charging document was legally defective for failing to provide specific factual details establishing the elements of conspiracy or sedition.
Trillanes argued that the charging document violated his constitutional right to be informed of the nature of the accusation.
Trillanes' motion, joined by co-accused Joselito Saracho, sought a dismissal of the case to prevent a protracted trial on a void charging document.

On February 10, 2020, the DOJ officially dismissed the cases of sedition, cyberlibel, libel, estafa, harboring a criminal, and obstruction of justice that had been filed against Vice President Leni Robredo and 23 other individuals.
The individuals whose cases were dismissed included senators, religious leaders, and lawyers.
The dismissal was based on a finding of lack of probable cause.
The case against Antonio Trillanes IV remained in limbo, with arraignment delays continuing due to motions to quash as of October 22, 2020.

The DOJ's resolution in the main case was later cited on February 10, 2025, which charged 11 respondents, including Advincula and Trillanes, with conspiracy to commit sedition under Article 141 of the Revised Penal Code.
In January 2021, Peter Joemel Advincula was charged with perjury for his contradictory statements regarding the videos.
In November 2021, Peter Joemel Advincula faced murder charges related to the so-called "Albay killings".
After being disqualified by the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) in October 2024, Peter Joemel Advincula filed as a nuisance candidate for the 2025 Senate election.
From the outset, Peter Joemel Advincula's background as a convicted fraudster with a six-year prison sentence, released early in 2017, cast a long shadow over his claims.
On May 8, 2019, Philippine National Police (PNP) Chief Gen. Oscar Albayalde publicly labeled Advincula an "information peddler".
PNP Chief Gen. Oscar Albayalde cited two prior instances where Advincula allegedly offered false information to police for sums ranging from ₱40,000 to ₱70,000.
Advincula failed to deliver or provided baseless claims in the prior instances where he allegedly offered false information to police.
PNP Chief Gen. Oscar Albayalde's characterization of Advincula directly contradicted the PNP chief's earlier statement that Advincula's initial accusations were "substantially accurate".
A detailed analysis by VERA Files Fact Check exposed recurring themes, missing information, and glaring inconsistencies across Advincula's various pronouncements and sworn statements.

In a December 2016 document he wrote, the "Sotto document," Advincula had accused officials from the preceding Aquino administration, including President Benigno Aquino III, Interior Secretary Mar Roxas, and Senator Leila de Lima, of having meetings with the drug syndicate figure Elizaldy "Zaldy" Co.
In his May 6, 2019, affidavit and press briefing detailing the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" videos, Aquino-era figures were entirely omitted from his list of accused patrons.
Advincula's focus shifted entirely to Duterte-aligned figures in his May 6, 2019, affidavit and press briefing.
Advincula named Paolo Duterte and Bong Go as the syndicate's patrons in the Davao area in his May 6, 2019, affidavit and press briefing.
The fact-checking analysis concluded that Advincula's accounts of the drug syndicate's structure and operations varied significantly across different affidavits and press conferences.
When the "matrix" report accusing journalists and opposition figures of plotting to oust President Duterte surfaced, the Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism (PCIJ) issued a strong denial.
PCIJ executive director Malou Mangahas stated that the organization did not receive any email from Vera Files president Ellen Tordesillas about the videos.
PCIJ executive director Malou Mangahas denied posting or distributing any stories related to the videos.
PCIJ executive director Malou Mangahas confirmed that the video was originally accessed by the public via YouTube.
PCIJ is a non-stock, independent media organization.
PCIJ executive director Malou Mangahas warned that those behind the "matrix" may have committed a crime by invading privacy through unauthorized access to journalists' emails.

The Department of Justice's dismissal of the sedition and other charges against Vice President Leni Robredo and 23 others on February 10, 2020, for lack of probable cause, represented a significant legal and political defeat for the executive branch.
The protracted legal battles, particularly the ongoing challenge to the charges against Antonio Trillanes IV, exemplified the long-term strategic cost of being targeted in such a manner.
Peter Joemel Advincula was charged with perjury in January 2021.
Peter Joemel Advincula was charged with murder in November 2021.

Peter Joemel Advincula's attempt to file as a nuisance candidate for the 2025 Senate election, even after being disqualified by the COMELEC, demonstrates his resilience and his ability to leverage the notoriety gained from the scandal to remain relevant.

The use of a prestigious institution like Ateneo de Manila University's server to host the videos added another layer of complexity, implicating academic and religious spaces in the political fray and raising questions about accountability.

8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_8 "January 8") – [Hanjin Heavy Industries and Construction Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanjin_Heavy_Industries_and_Construction_Philippines "Hanjin Heavy Industries and Construction Philippines") (HHIC Phil) files for corporate rehabilitation after declaring bankruptcy. It is the biggest bankruptcy in the Philippines surpassing the more than $386 million financial losses in the country related to the [Lehman Brothers bankruptcy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehman_Brothers_bankruptcy "Lehman Brothers bankruptcy") of 2008.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-1) HHIC defaulted its $412 million loan credited to five local banking firms.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-2) * [January 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_10 "January 10"): * President Duterte signs Republic Act. No. 11188, providing special protection of children in armed conflict.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-3) * Maia Santos Deguito, the former bank manager of [Rizal Commercial Banking Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rizal_Commercial_Banking_Corporation "Rizal Commercial Banking Corporation") (RCBC) is convicted of money laundering in connection with the [$81-million cyber heist on Bangladesh's central bank in 2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Bank_robbery "Bangladesh Bank robbery").[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-4) * [January 21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_21 "January 21") – A [plebiscite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Bangsamoro_autonomy_plebiscite "2019 Bangsamoro autonomy plebiscite") takes place with the majority of voters ratifying the [Bangsamoro Organic Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangsamoro_Organic_Law "Bangsamoro Organic Law") creating the [Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangsamoro_Autonomous_Region_in_Muslim_Mindanao "Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao") and abolishing the [Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_Region_in_Muslim_Mindanao "Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao").[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-5) [Cotabato City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotabato_City "Cotabato City") also votes to join the new autonomous region while in [Isabela City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabela,_Basilan "Isabela, Basilan") in [Basilan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilan "Basilan") rejects its inclusion to the region.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-7) * [January 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_24 "January 24") – The [International Union for Conservation of Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Union_for_Conservation_of_Nature "International Union for Conservation of Nature") (IUCN) places [tawilis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardinella_tawilis "Sardinella tawilis") on the list of endangered species.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-8) * [January 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_27 "January 27"): * At least 20 people are killed while 111 people are injured after [explosions rock the Cathedral of Our Lady of Mount Carmel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Jolo_Cathedral_bombings "2019 Jolo Cathedral bombings") in [Jolo, Sulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolo,_Sulu "Jolo, Sulu").[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-12) * [January 28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_28 "January 28") – Lawmakers propose to lower the [age of criminal responsibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_of_criminal_responsibility "Age of criminal responsibility"), sparking outrage. * [February 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_6 "February 6") – The second round of the [Bangamoro Organic Law plebiscite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Bangsamoro_autonomy_plebiscite "2019 Bangsamoro autonomy plebiscite") is held with voters in 67 barangays in [Cotabato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotabato "Cotabato") and six towns in [Lanao del Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lanao_del_Norte "Lanao del Norte") deciding if they are in favor of their localities joining the proposed Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-13)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-14) The 63 barangays in Cotabato vote to join the new region while the six municipalities in Lanao del Norte, despite approving the motion, fail to join after the rest of the province rejects their inclusion to the region.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-15)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-16) * [February 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_13 "February 13") – [Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler") CEO [Maria Ressa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Ressa "Maria Ressa") is arrested by the [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_/(Philippines/) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)") (NBI) for [cyber libel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cybercrime_Prevention_Act_of_2012 "Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012") upon orders from Manila Regional Trial Court Branch 46.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-17)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-ReferenceA-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-19) She posts bail the next day. Ressa claims that her right to due process was violated, since she was not informed of the complaint against her. She also describes her arrest as an "abuse of power" and "weaponization of the law".[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-ReferenceA-18) Ressa's arrest is condemned by journalists, organizations, and influential figures from the Philippines and abroad, describing it as an attack on press freedom.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-20)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-21)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-ReferenceB-22) Presidential Spokesperson [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") denies that the government was trying to silence press freedom.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-ReferenceB-22) President Duterte has repeatedly labeled Rappler as "[fake news](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fake_news "Fake news")" as he perceives the online news site to be too critical of his administration.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-23)[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-24) However, the libel complaint had been filed by businessman Wilfredo Keng regarding a Rappler article published in May 2012 (updated in February 2014) where Keng was alleged to have lent a vehicle to Chief Justice [Renato Corona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Corona "Renato Corona"), who was undergoing an impeachment trial at the time.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-25) The article also links Keng to human trafficking and drug smuggling.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-26) * [February 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_14 "February 14") – President Duterte signs Republic Act No. 11201, creating the [Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Human_Settlements_and_Urban_Development "Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development").[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-27) * [February 22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_22 "February 22") – President Duterte signs the [Tulong-Trabaho Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tulong-Trabaho_Act&action=edit&redlink=1 "Tulong-Trabaho Act (page does not exist)") (Republic Act 11230), mandating free access to [technical-vocational education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVET_/(technical_and_vocational_education_and_training/) "TVET (technical and vocational education and training)").[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-28) * [February 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_26 "February 26") – The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao formally established and the [Bangsamoro Transition Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangsamoro_Transition_Authority "Bangsamoro Transition Authority") (BTA) is constituted.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-29)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-30)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-31) * Since [March 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_6 "March 6") – Numerous areas across [Metro Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Manila "Metro Manila"), estimated to be 52,000 households by [Manila Water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_Water "Manila Water"), [experience water scarcity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Metro_Manila_water_crisis "2019 Metro Manila water crisis").[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-32) Manila Water COO Geodino Carpio cites the delay of water infrastructure projects, such as the constructions of a [wastewater treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wastewater_treatment "Wastewater treatment") plant in [Cardona, Rizal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardona,_Rizal "Cardona, Rizal") and the [Kaliwa Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Centennial_Water_Source-Kaliwa_Dam_Project "New Centennial Water Source-Kaliwa Dam Project") in [Tanay, Rizal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanay,_Rizal "Tanay, Rizal"), for the issue.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-33) Manila Water also noted the critically low levels of the [La Mesa Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Mesa_Dam_and_Reservoir "La Mesa Dam and Reservoir"), its lowest level in 12 years, which the company relies on as their emergency supply of water source.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-34) * [March 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_10 "March 10") – [Murder of Christine Silawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_Christine_Silawan "Murder of Christine Silawan") in [Lapu-Lapu City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lapu-Lapu_City "Lapu-Lapu City"), [Cebu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cebu "Cebu").[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-35)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-36) * [March 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_15 "March 15") – Former Ombudsman [Conchita Carpio-Morales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conchita_Carpio-Morales "Conchita Carpio-Morales") and former Secretary of Foreign Affairs [Albert del Rosario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_del_Rosario "Albert del Rosario") file a case in the [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") (ICC) against Chinese President [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping") and other Chinese government officials for alleged [crimes against humanity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimes_against_humanity "Crimes against humanity").[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-37) The complaint cited environmental damage in the [South China Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_China_Sea "South China Sea") due to land reclamation, occupation of islands, and destructive fishing activities conducted by China.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-38) The communication was delivered to the ICC two days before the Philippines' ICC withdrawal became effective.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-39)[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-40)[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_in_the_Philippines#cite_note-41) * [March 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_17 "March 17") – The Philippines formally withdraws from the [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") after the country's withdrawal notification was received by the [Secretary-General of the United Calida: Bikoy’s Narcolist videos published using Ateneo server
==============================================================

Aug 20, 2019 5:00 PM PHT

[Lian Buan](https://www.rappler.com/author/lian-buan/)

SUMMARY

This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

![Image 1: Calida: Bikoy’s Narcolist videos published using Ateneo server](https://www.rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/5BF191A5E0874F74BB7F508EB861EC3A/img/647F87AA91F84B12857B30E0579D91EA/bikoy-doj-sedition-august-9-2019-001.jpg)

Rappler.com

INFO

_'Could Advincula stage the grand scheme Project Sodoma all by himself?' says the solicitor general_

MANILA, Philippines – Solicitor General Jose Calida said on Tuesday, August 20, that the viral Ang Totoong Narcolist videos that accused President Rodrigo Duterte of drug links were published using the servers of Ateneo de Manila University (ADMU).

“Thereafter, the ‘Ang Totoong Narco-List’ videos were released online. They were all released using the server of Ateneo de Manila University where Respondent Peter Joemel Advincula was safely housed and hidden,” said Calida in an omnibus comment submitted to the Department of Justice (DOJ) on Tuesday.

Calida’s claims echoed the affidavit of Peter Joemel Advincula alias Bikoy, who is the government’s star witness in the inciting to sedition complaint it filed against Vice President Leni Robredo, key figures of the opposition, noted lawyers and high officials of the Catholic Church.

Advincula had said in his affidavit: _“Ginamit ko ang main server na may SSID na Guest 1 na naka attach sa Management Information System ng ADMU sa loob ng Room 2C, ADMU University Dorm, Faculty Housing, ADMU Compound na inuupahan noon ni Father Alejo.”_

(I used the main server of SSID Guest 1 which is attache to the Management Information System of ADMU inside Room 2C, ADMU University Dorm, Faculty Housing, ADMU compound being rented then by Father Albert Alejo.)

The CIDG did not initially submit physical evidence, including supposed electronic traces, and relied only on Advincula’s affidavit – which is the final narrative [after two sensational flip-flops since 2016.](https://www.rappler.com/newsbreak/in-depth/237169-biggest-flip-flops-bikoy-government-star-witness?fbclid=IwAR2bCHcJvy5cRs8bFTXfjSibxmDEAfiqrecKV1ZzKhDLQKU05GQDqf5dYbs)

[](https://www.rappler.com/newsbreak/in-depth/237169-biggest-flip-flops-bikoy-government-star-witness?fbclid=IwAR2bCHcJvy5cRs8bFTXfjSibxmDEAfiqrecKV1ZzKhDLQKU05GQDqf5dYbs)The CIDG was given until August 23 to submit them. Robredo and other respondents were allowed by the DOJ to submit their counter-affidavits only after they have received the additional evidence.

**Key dates and Ateneo**

Advincula claimed that several people, known publicly for their work in the offices of key Liberal Party (LP) members, helped him shoot the videos inside the Jesuit Communications Building or Jescom in Ateneo. He claimed to be in possession of receipts of the said individuals buying the gadgets for the video production.

Former Ateneo president Fr Jose Ramon Villarin [had said in an earlier statement](https://web.facebook.com/ateneodemanila/posts/10161674043815153) that “Ateneo did not convene or organize any of the meetings alleged by Advincula to have taken place on campus.”

We have reached out to the Ateneo’s Public Affairs Office for a reaction on Calida’s new claim.

Here is a timeline that we have culled from affidavits so far:

*   **August 2018 –** Advincula claims Project Sodoma starts meeting from this date.
*   **February 9, 2019 –**  Caloocan Bishop Pablo Virgilio David [admits meeting Advincula](https://www.rappler.com/nation/237909-bishop-david-refused-bikoy-request-church-sanctuary) inside his residence in Caloocan. Advincula, David says, is accompanied on that date to Caloocan by Jesuit priest Father Albert Alejo. 
*   **March 29, 2019 –** Advincula claims that they start shooting on this date the ‘Ang Totoong Narcolist’ videos inside Jescom.
*   **April 1, 2019 –** The first Ang Totoong Narcolist video is uploaded.
*   **April 22, 2019 –** The 5th and supposedly last Ang Totoong Narcolist video was uploaded.
*   **April 24, 2019 –** Lingayen-Dagupan Archbishop Socrates Villegas [admit](https://www.rappler.com/nation/237827-villegas-affidavit-denies-bikoy-links-admits-meeting-him-once)s to meeting Advincula at the Jesuit Residence in Ateneo on this date, at 8:30 am. Advincula claims in his affidavit that they uploaded a “stitched-together” video on April 24. Advincula say he could not recall the time.
*   **May 6, 2019 –** Advincula first appears in public on this date inside the Integrated Bar of the Philippines, still standing by the anti-Duterte Bikoy videos.
*   **May 23, 2019** – Advincula retracts all his accusations against Duterte and turns the tables on the opposition [at a press conference](https://www.rappler.com/nation/231362-pnp-hosts-bikoy-press-briefing-after-calling-him-liar) by the Philippine National Police (PNP).

“Could Advincula, a criminal runaway without a penny to his name and with just a high school diploma, stage the grand scheme Project Sodoma all by himself, and use and manipulate respondents – who are some of the highest officials of the land, the alleged seasoned litigators and practitioners of the legal profession, the clergies of the Catholic Church as his unwitting, unsuspecting, and innocent pawns in his own macabre game of thrones?” Calida said.

The pleading asked the DOJ to junk all questions of legality of the respondents, including the Office of the Solicitor General or OSG’s authority to participate in the preliminary investigation.

The Free Legal Assistance Group (FLAG), representing respondent-lawyers Ted Te, Chel Diokno and Erin Tañada, [has moved to disqualify](https://www.rappler.com/nation/238040-flag-lawyers-move-disqualify-osg-inciting-sedition-probe) the OSG in the investigation citing the office’s limited function in appeal cases in court only.

The next hearing of the DOJ is on September 6. – **Rappler.com**

PCIJ: Those behind ‘matrix’ report may have committed crime, violated freedom
=============================================================================

By ANNA FELICIA BAJO, GMA News

**Published** April 22, 2019 10:08pm  

The people who came up with a "matrix" accusing several groups and individuals of a plot to oust President Rodrigo Duterte may have committed a crime and violated fundamental freedoms, the Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism (PCIJ) said.

"The Manila Times story admits to a crime that may have been committed, and fundamental freedoms that may have been violated. It offers tacit admission that these 'experts,' apparently working with the Office of the President, had invaded the privacy of the emails and correspondence of journalists now being singled out," PCIJ executive director Malou Mangahas said in a statement.

Mangahas also emphasized that the PCIJ did not receive any email from Vera Files president Ellen Tordesillas about "Ang Totoong Narcolist," a series of videos claiming that the Duterte family has links to illegal drugs.

It was stated in the report that Tordesillas was the "nexus and distributor" of materials from "Bikoy," the person in the videos making the allegations who claimed to be a former member of a drug syndicate.

"PCIJ has neither posted nor distributed any stories or commentaries on the 'narcolist video' of 'Bikoy.' The video was posted on YouTube from where the news media and citizens got to watch it," Mangahas said.

"That is where the so-called 'cybercrime experts' of the unnamed 'highly placed source in the Office of the President' should look instead," she added.

Mangahas also noted that the matrix had linked at least five individuals to the PCIJ who are no longer employed at the media firm.

She further stated that as a non-stock, not-for-profit independent media organization, the PCIJ has been funded in different ways, including by revenues from the sale of publications and video, contributions from PCIJ patrons, interest income from an endowment fund from the Ford Foundation, and grants for projects from both local and foreign sources.

"Foreign funding is not equivalent to foreign ownership of for-profit media. Truth be told, government agencies are the biggest recipients of foreign funding from the United States, Japan, China, Australia, and other multilateral and bilateral agencies," Mangahas said.

She added that Rigoberto Tiglao, who writes for The Manila Times, was a co-founder and the first treasurer of the PCIJ, and that he had helped raise seed money for the PCIJ’s operations initially from the Asia Foundation and the Ford Foundation.

She also said PCIJ seminars since 2014 have been attended by hundreds of reporters and editors from various media organizations, including about a dozen from the Manila Times.

**Hilarious**

Many of the individuals named in the report as being part of the supposed "ouster plot" have denied any involvement in any plot to remove the President.

VERA Files' [Tordesillas called it "hilarious"](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/news/nation/691983/vera-files-on-ouster-plot-phl-in-big-trouble-if-this-is-the-kind-of-intel-duterte-gets/story/) and said, "\[I\]f this is the kind of intelligence report that the President gets and bases his actions and policies on, the country is in big trouble."

Bayan Muna's Neri Colmenares and Representative Carlos Zarate [called it "absurd" and "ridiculous."](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/news/nation/691978/colmenares-zarate-deny-involvement-in-lsquo-ridiculous-rsquo-alleged-ouster-plot/story/)

"Parang silang mga sirang plaka na paulit-ulit ng kasinungalingan," said Zarate.

News site Rappler said that the matrix [was an example of "how not to write an investigative report,"](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/news/nation/691986/rappler-criticizes-matrix-report-an-example-of-how-not-to-write-investigative-report/story/) while the National Union of People's Lawyers [called it "absolutely false," ludicrous and baseless.](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/news/nation/691980/nupl-slams-link-to-alleged-duterte-ouster-plot/story/)

Malacañang has backed the matrix report, with presidential spokesman Salvador Panelo [saying that it should be believed because Duterte had validated the information for the report.](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/news/nation/691981/palace-backs-report-linking-investigative-journos-to-bikoy-destabilization/story/)

Panelo also said that he was actually the one who was supposed to release the "matrix," but that the Manila Times had beaten him to it. **— Dona Magsino/BM, GMA News**

3.content:
![Image 1](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/DD026F08A0224E068F2FFA864BE74266/desktop-header-2.png)

Peter Joemel Advincula, the man known as Bikoy, has told many versions of a sensational tale about drugs and the country’s most powerful

* * *

Published 9:54 AM, August 12, 2019

MANILA, Philippines – With the Duterte government backing him, [Peter Joemel Advincula](https://www.rappler.com/newsbreak/profiles/229909-alias-bikoy-from-seminarian-ex-convict-whistleblower) has become one of the country's most powerful storytellers.

So potent is his tale that it has given flesh to a complaint of inciting to sedition against the country’s Vice President Leni Robredo, along with other recognizable figures of the opposition Liberal Party (LP).

The Department of Justice (DOJ) started on Friday, August 9, its preliminary investigation into the inciting to sedition complaint against Robredo, two incumbent senators, two former senators, one former congressman, a former Cabinet secretary, 6 senatorial candidates, and the former head of the Catholic Bishops Conference of the Philippines, among others.

The police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) seeks to jail Robredo and the key opposition members for up to 6 years over what they call “ [Project Sodoma](https://www.rappler.com/nation/236211-doj-start-sending-subpoenas-robredo-lp-lawmakers-bikoy-complaint) ,” a supposed destabilization plot against the Duterte administration with Advincula as one of its pillars.

Lawyer Larry Gadon, himself a former senatorial candidate, also floated the idea of impeaching Robredo on the basis of a possible indictment from the DOJ, and not even a conviction.

Much of it will depend on the story of the man who came to be known as "Bikoy."

Since 2016, Bikoy’s story has altered and morphed, its characters changing circumstances and motivations.

Before taking him in as their star witness, police chief Oscar Albayalde described Bikoy as an “ [information peddler](https://www.rappler.com/nation/229974-pnp-dismisses-bikoy-information-peddler) .”

We track his story beginning December 2016 and list the most glaring holes in his accounts. It begins with a sensational tale set in an underground room in a Bicol resort and a made-for-movies account of CCTV footage catching no other than the Philippine president supposedly taking an envelope and flying off in a private plane.

Under CIDG custody, Advincula has now discarded the entire underground story, and has pivoted completely to Project Sodoma against the opposition.

To see the changing testimonies of Advincula, press, hold, drag to the left or to the right, and release the sliders in the middle of the illustrations.

![Image 2](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/509313A167034FBCACEA2420E8AFE9BE/desktop-q1-02.png)

![Image 3](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/0507F38D553F42F8AD893C4EB9487A3B/desktop-q1-01.png)

**I. Underground room in Misibis Bay**
--------------------------------------

Back in 2016, Advincula was just one of thousands of prisoners inside the New Bilibid Prison. He was serving a 6-year sentence for estafa handed down in 2012. By December, he had an idea for a way out.

He reached out to the office of Senator [Vicente “Tito” Sotto III](https://www.rappler.com/nation/229993-sotto-says-bikoy-had-same-drug-allegations-vs-aquino-administration-2016) , and told them the story of how he met Bicolano business tycoon Zaldy Co.

Advincula said Co hired him to be a technical man for the so-called Quadrangle Drug Group he claimed was based in Misibis Bay resort in Bicol. There, Advincula was supposedly given access to the CCTV room of underground quarters of the syndicate he called the "Central House."

Advincula also told Sotto’s team that aside from minding the cameras, he was also a leader of a drug delivery team.

What he claimed to have seen in the monitors could be damaging to any presidency: that in April 2011, former president Benigno "Noynoy" Aquino III, his justice secretary at the time, Leila de Lima, his executive secretary Paquito Ochoa Jr, and Mar Roxas paid repeated visits to the syndicate’s headquarters.

" _Nakita ko din po o nahagip din ng Camera 36 ng aming CCTV footage sa technical room ng sindikato ang pag-abot ng dalawang brown envelope ni Elizalde Co kay dating Pangulong Noynoy Aquino, na iniaabot naman ni dating Pangulong Noynoy Aquino kay undersecretary Ricardo Puno.......Hapon ng araw ding yuon nilisan ni Pangulong Aquino ang Misibis Bay lulan ng private helicopter na pagmamay-ari po ni Elizaldy Co_ ," Advincula said in this affidavit.

(I saw through Camera 36 of our CCTV footage in the syndicate’s technical room that Elizalde Co handed over two brown envelopes to former president Noynoy Aquino, who then handed them to undersecretary Ricardo Puno...That afternoon, President Aquino left Misibis Bay, aboard a private helicopter owned by Elizaldy Co.)

At the height of the Bikoy issue in May 2019, Sotto came out to say Advincula had approached him in 2016 but that he found his claims suspicious.

During that time, De Lima was being investigated by the House justice committee for supposed participation in the drug trade inside Bilibid. Her bodyguard Ronnie Dayan was her alleged bagman.

“He wanted to be a witness against Senator De Lima,” Sotto said.

Advincula was never invited as a witness in the 2016 public trial of De Lima, his name unknown until he became Bikoy.

**II. Becoming Bikoy**
----------------------

![Image 4](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/883D326E7AA74479934DD1F26683152D/desktop-q2-02.png)

![Image 5](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/2E682AB629664901B12DCE08819FE1C7/desktop-q2-01.png)

This anti-Aquino administration narrative was overhauled in 2019, when Advincula assumed the character he is most known as today. He was already a free man, but he said he felt he needed to say something about the Duterte administration.

He shrouded himself with a hood, spoke in the safety of shadows and called himself “Bikoy.”

In this new story, Advincula introduced himself as a former member of a Bicol-based “ [Quadrangle Drug Syndicate](https://www.rappler.com/nation/227352-malacanang-dismisses-totoong-narco-list-video-black-propaganda) ,” but this time he claimed to be in charge of managing financial documents and scanning supposed tattoos that senior syndicate members bore to claim their monthly shares in drug money.

He retained Ochoa, Puno, and added former Aquino cabinet secretaries Proceso Alcala and Ramon Paje as cast members. But he went on to hurl accusations against people close to President Rodrigo Duterte.

“Paolo Duterte, Veronica Salvador, Bong Go, at Mans Carpio. _Sila po ang main players from Davao side na lumalabas sa mga dokumentong hawak ko_ (From the documents that I hold, they appear to be the main players from the Davao side),” Advincula said in episode 4 of the video series, calling them part of the so-called Tausug drug group.

Advincula claimed that he saw Paolo Duterte and Go inside Misibis Bay repeatedly, and that he himself scanned their supposed syndicate tattoos.

He again accused Bicol tycoon Elizaldy Co of keeping the drug syndicate in his Misibis Bay resort, and then accused other Bicolano politicians of being part of the Quadrangle Group, namely:

*   Edgardo Tallado
*   Krunimar Escudero
*   Victor Rosales
*   Luis Villafuerte
*   Thomas Enrile
*   Fernando Gonzales
*   Joseph Cua
*   Tess Rañola

**III. The untold story of 'Oplan Yellow'**
-------------------------------------------

![Image 6](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/5FD9A8304B8B46068586F1AECAA6E5C3/desktop-q3-02.png)

![Image 7](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/3068935FCF7E411A9D107EE4A897CF83/desktop-q3-01.png)

His accusations in the video are only part of a longer unsigned affidavit by Bikoy and obtained by Rappler.

" _Sa bawat pagpupulong ng mga patron at patriarchal sa Quadrangle Central House ay naroon parati sila Paolo Duterte, Bong Go, at James Baay kasama ang iba pang Chinese nationalities, businessmen, at matataas na police officials ng aming rehiyon at maging sa lugar ng Davao City na pawang mga kasama nila Paolo Duterte_ ," said Advincula in the affidavit dated January 25, 2019.

(In every meeting of the patrons and patriarchs of the Quadriangle Central House, there was Paolo Duterte, Bong Go, and James Baay, with other Chinese nationals, businessmen, and high-ranking police officials of our region and Davao City, who accompanied Paolo Duterte.)

He expanded it to another narrative, which included "Oplan Yellow" in which he claimed to have seen President Rodrigo Duterte himself inside Bilibid during his detention, plotting drug charges against his fierce critic De Lima.

Advincula said in the affidavit that he was convicted of large-scale illegal recruitment that sent him to Bilibid on May 27, 2016.

By August 2016, Advincula claimed to have seen former justice secretary Vitaliano Aguirre, former interior secretary Ismael Sueno, and the police chief at the time, and now senator Ronald "Bato" Dela Rosa, enter Bilibid to meet with drug convicts.

Advincula claimed to have been part of a secretariat in the Inmate's Complaints Information and Assistance Center (ICIAC) of Bilibid's Medium Security compound, where he said, he prepared some "Oplan Yellow" documents.

" _Sa ilang pagkakataon ay kami pa mismo ng aking mga kasamahang technical secretariat ang tumatawag sa mga nabanggit na contact numbers upang magbigay ng update o situationary development o maging sa iba pang idagdag ng pahayag tungkol sa aming inihahandang mga scripted sinumpaang salaysay ng mga high-profile inmates at convicted drug lords na magsasalita laban kay Sen Leila de Lima_ ," Advincula said.

(At times, my companions and I from the technical secretariat called the numbers to give updates and situationary developments and additions about the scripted sworn statements we were preparing for the high-profile inmates and convicted drug lords against Senator Leila de Lima.)

Advincula added: " _Sabado, ikalawang linggo ng Setyembre taong 2016 sa pagitan ng oras na ika-walo at ika-siyam ng gabi.....may sunud-sunod na pumasok na mga sasakyan sa Medium Security Compound lulan ang Pangulong Rodrigo Duterte kasama sila Secretary Bong Go, Secretary Salvador Panelo, Secretary Jose Calida at iilan pang matataas na opisyal ng Office of the President at Presidential Security Group_ ."

(On Saturday, in the second week of September, year 2016, between 6 and 8 pm...there was a convoy of cars at the Medium Security Compound carrying President Rodrigo Duterte, with Secretary Bong Go, Secretary Salvador Panelo, Secretary Jose Calida, and other high-ranking officials of the Office of the President and the Presidential Security Group.)

**IV. The turnaround**
----------------------

![Image 8](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/4675BE690D894C74BA74F1E7CC9D1D9F/desktop-q4-02.png)

![Image 9](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/DF6A778D289E4E1C984EBA537BA31275/desktop-q4-01.png)

As his accusations against the Duterte administration sparked controversy, Advincula showed up in a press conference held at the [Integrated Bar of the Philippines](https://www.rappler.com/nation/236122-ibp-mulls-disclosing-bikoy-presscon-details-authorities) (IBP) headquarters on May 6.

There, he asked for help to sue Paolo Duterte and Go.

But two days later on May 8, Advincula stood at the pedestal of the PNP in Camp Crame, baring another grand twist to his story.

Advincula retracted all his public statements against the Dutertes and Go, and then accused their political nemesis, former senator Antonio Trillanes IV, of masterminding the anti-administration accusations.

He claimed that it was the Liberal Party who was behind the _Ang Totoong Narco List_ (The Real Narco List) videos, with involvement reaching up to Vice President Leni Robredo.

Trillanes has denied Advincula's claims, but admitted to meeting him in August 2018 to vet his claims.

" _Pinakinggan ko siya, subalit nakulangan at naguluhan ako sa mga detalye at isinantabi ko at tuluyan ko nang kinalimutan_ ," the senator said.

(I listened to him, but I found his testimony lacking and confusing. I set it aside and totally forgot about it.)

Before he could start a new narrative, however, Advincula had to clean a messy plate.

He disowned his two previous affidavits, and admitted that everything about the underground room in Misibis Bay was false.

But in retracting, he made another accusation that should interest investigators if they truly believe in Advincula – that there was a plot of sorts from within the Bureau of Corrections to jail De Lima for drugs.

" _Isinubo lang sa akin ito ng mga tauhan ng Bureau of Corrections_ (This was only fed to me by the people of the Bureau of Corrections)," Advincula said, referring to purported documents on the illegal drug trade being linked to De Lima.

“ _During that time sa BuCor kasi kailangan magkaroon ng direct link na mismong si Sen De Lima talaga ay mayroon mismong sindikato ng droga...pinagtitiwala ko na muna sa otoridad 'yun but they are the personnel of the Bucor na may matinding galit din kay Sen De Lima_ ,” he said during his press conference in Camp Crame.

(During that time at the BuCor, there was a need to establish a direct link between Senator De Lima herself and the drug syndicate...I only entrusted it to authorities, but the people of BuCor held an intense grudge against Senator De Lima.)

**V. CIDG affidavits inconsistent**
-----------------------------------

![Image 10](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/99451EA2C56142EF815F1659E6A40840/desktop-q5-02.png)

![Image 11](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/FB62219B3BC5406BB34F494A23C36B95/desktop-q5-01.png)

Advincula has executed two CIDG affidavits that link the Project Sodoma conspiracy with the opposition, one dated May 29, 2019, and the other, dated July 17, 2019. The July 17 version is the one that was submitted to the DOJ when the CIDG filed the complaint of inciting to sedition.

Even in these affidavits, Advincula made contradictory claims.

In both, Advincula said he first asked Father Ruben Reyes for financial help in August 2018. Advincula said he knows Reyes because the latter, a Jesuit, served as the chaplain of the Naga City Jail where he served time before Bilibid.

Advincula claimed Reyes linked him up with other priests associated with the [Ateneo](https://www.rappler.com/nation/232381-bishop-david-slams-bikoy-lying-linking-to-trillanes) – all of whom are also respondents in the sedition complaint.

Advincula said that through the Jesuit priests, he met Trillanes on August 29, 9 pm, at the Jesuit Residence inside Ateneo.

In the first affidavit, Advincula said he met Trillanes again on February 9 at the residence of Caloocan Bishop Pablo Virgilio David. But in the second affidavit, Advincula said Trillanes participated in the meeting at the Bishop's residence only by calling Father Albert Alejo through ProtonMail. ProtonMail is a secure email service and does not have a call feature.

On October 11, 2018, Advincula said he met top aides of Trillanes at the Loyola School of Theology where he was handed his 2016 affidavit – the one involving Aquino, De Lima, Roxas etc – but revised and replaced with Duterte and Go.

" _Pinag-usapan namin ang dokumento na ibinigay ko sa kanila ni Senator Trillanes noong nakaraang Agosto subalit nakita ko na may ibang version na ito at ang tinutukoy na ay ang pamilyang Duterte at si Bong Go,_ " said Advincula in both affidavits.

(We spoke about the document I gave to Senator Trillanes and the others in August, but I saw that there was a different version that now referred to the Duterte family and Bong Go.)

**VI. Targeting the VP**
------------------------

![Image 12](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/3BB38E588DD8402DBFBCA37797F4902D/desktop-q6-02.png)

![Image 13](https://rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/DCD463B689EE4943BD3E18CD2B992A1E/img/C8DA62A40703477D82CFD05ECD14A197/desktop-q6-01.png)

Advincula claimed he met Robredo on March 4 at Leong Hall inside Ateneo, along with [Otso Diretso candidates](https://www.rappler.com/newsbreak/in-depth/232120-after-tough-loss-otso-diretso-eyes-set-elections-2022) , with only Roxas missing.

In his first affidavit in May 2019, he claimed Robredo dropped by and spent 10 minutes in the meeting. In the 2nd affidavit last July, he claimed Robredo participated in the meeting.

Advincula said in Filipino: "On March 4, 2019, around 4 pm, we had a meeting inside Leong Hall at ADMU, with candidates of Otso Diretso, namely Chel Diokno, Gary Alejano, Pilo Hilbay, Romy Macalintal, Samira Gutoc, Bam Aquino, and Erin Tañada. Present there too were Father Alejo, Vicente Romano, Yolly Ong, Dan Sungco, and Vice President Leni Robredo."

The Otso Diretso candidates and the Office of the Vice President (OVP) have denied Advincula's claims.

Alejano said the March 4 Ateneo narrative is convenient because the candidates were on campus for the Rappler senatorial forum.

"Bikoy's allegation against me is a complete lie and ridiculous. Again and again, I categorically state that I don't know Bikoy and have never met him. _Tinaon niya ang kanyang kwento ng meeting daw niya_ sa Otso Diretso (8D) on March 4, 2019 where there was a Rappler Senatorial Forum in Leong Hall in Ateneo attended by the members of 8D. I must emphasize, though, that such activity was well covered by media and witnessed by many people both inside and outside the venue. Certainly, the truth will come out," said Alejano.

The two CIDG affidavits in May and July 2019 made mention of electronic traces of Advincula's communication with the people he is accusing, key cards of the apartments that he claimed were the Project Sodoma bases, as well as receipts for when they supposedly bought gadgets to shoot the _Ang Totoong Narco List_ videos.

Witness credibility and corroboration are strong considerations of prosecutors when determining probable cause. The DOJ had once before cleared a drug suspect because of inaccuracies of an illiterate witness.

The DOJ wants to haul into its rooms the second highest official of the land, members of Congress and the Catholic Church – and line them up against a government star witness who has flip-flopped many times over. **– Rappler.com

Bikoy’s statements ‘substantially accurate, supported by evidence’—PNP chief
============================================================================

By: [Cathrine Gonzales](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/byline/cathrine-gonzales) - Reporter / [@cgonzalesINQ](https://www.twitter.com/@cgonzalesINQ)

[INQUIRER.net](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/source/inquirer-net) / 11:32 AM July 25, 2019

Share:

[![Image 24: Copy Link](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/copy-link.svg)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1146140/bikoys-statements-substantially-accurate-supported-by-evidence-pnp-chief#)

[![Image 26: Bookmark](blob:https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/76f70cba1a4985ff842bd808acca549c)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1146140/bikoys-statements-substantially-accurate-supported-by-evidence-pnp-chief#)

[![Image 28: Facebook](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/fb-share.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1146140%2Fbikoys-statements-substantially-accurate-supported-by-evidence-pnp-chief)

[![Image 30: X](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/x-share.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1146140%2Fbikoys-statements-substantially-accurate-supported-by-evidence-pnp-chief)

MANILA, Philippines — Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Gen. Oscar Albayalde has maintained that the accusations of Peter Joemel Advincula or “Bikoy” in the narcolist videos  were “substantially accurate.”

Albayalde said Thursday that the CIDG, which filed sedition and piles of other criminal charges against Vice President Leni Robredo and 35 other personalities tagged in the release of the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” (The Real Narcolist) series, also had other evidence that supported Advincula’s affidavit.

**READ: [Sedition case filed vs Robredo, 35 others over ‘Bikoy’ videos](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1143292/pnp-cidg-files-sedition-case-vs-robredo-over-totoong-narcolist-video#ixzz5ueRTvA9k)**

_Article continues after this advertisement_

“Remember, the statements of Bikoy or Peter Joemel Advincula accordingly were substantially accurate because they are supported by other documentary evidence and other sources,” he said in an interview with ABS-CBN News Channel.
